source.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock V

teaching.hint: Which information about an unfinished transaction changes the effect of the next price?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Flat, long, and short positions have different price exposure. Completed transaction count and position type summarize all relevant past decisions.
solution_outline.approach: Scan days with arrays for each completed count and the three position types. From yesterday states, wait, open long or short from flat, or close a position into flat with count increased. Initially only flat with zero completed is reachable. Return the maximum final flat value over counts through k.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: After a day, each state stores the largest cash attainable with that exact completed count and open-position type; open positions carry their opening cash effect but are not final profits.
solution_outline.correctness: Every legal schedule performs at most one action per day and follows precisely these position transitions. Reading previous-day states forces closing after opening and prevents a same-day close/reopen. Conversely every DP transition path describes a legal schedule. For a fixed state, greater cash dominates under every continuation, so retaining its maximum loses no optimum. Only flat final states contain completed transactions.
solution_outline.complexity: O(nk) time and O(k) auxiliary space; profit totals require 64-bit arithmetic.
solution_outline.pitfall: Updating states in place can allow closing and reopening on the same day in violation of the contract.

common_wrong_turns: Updating states in place can allow closing and reopening on the same day in violation of the contract.
source_fidelity_notes: Retained both normal and short transactions, strictly later close, no shared close/open day, at-most count, and completed final positions.
